text:
Registered residential sales reached 11,316 units valued at AED 33,892,693,593 over the last four weeks, representing a 7.0 percent increase in volume and 23.3 percent growth in value compared to the prior period. Mortgage registrations totaled 4,572, which are tracked separately from sales. The median residential price per square foot rose 1.1 percent to AED 1,693. Off-plan transactions accounted for 58.0 percent of the total, down from 61.5 percent in the previous four weeks.

The rental market recorded 89,438 Ejari contracts with a renewal share of 51.8 percent. The median annual residential rent stood at AED 69,498. Top performing areas by sales volume included Dubai South with 3,431 units and Jumeirah Village Circle with 2,283 units over the last twelve weeks. Business Bay showed a 3.3 percent decline in median price per square foot, while Al Hebiah Fifth recorded a 2.3 percent increase.

Price momentum varied significantly across communities. Al Yufrah 1 led gains with a 43.5 percent increase in median price per square foot over twelve weeks, followed by Dubai Industrial City at 12.5 percent. Conversely, Palm Jumeirah experienced a 13.8 percent decline, and Liwan fell by 13.3 percent. Highest estimated gross yields were observed in Zaabeel First at 9.1 percent and International City Phase 1 at 8.6 percent, both for flats.

Investors should monitor the 1,058 anomalous sales priced more than 35 percent away from comparable medians in the last 60 days. These figures are derived from registered DLD data and Ejari contracts using medians and benchmark filters that exclude bulk deals, partial shares, mortgages, gifts, and statistical outliers.

facts.ranking_rule: communities with at least 30 eligible sales in both 12-week windows; yields also need 30 rent contracts of the same property type
